about.title: Personal Injury Help in Santa Ana, California
about.longDescription: As the Orange County seat, Santa Ana packs dense neighborhoods, a busy civic center and constant freeway traffic into a compact, walkable city. Public records show more than 1,700 injury collisions here in 2025, leaving nearly 2,400 people hurt, with reported crashes tending to peak on Friday evenings. The I-5 (Santa Ana Freeway) cuts through the city while surface routes like First Street and Bristol Street carry heavy pedestrian and vehicle traffic. Whether you were injured in a wreck, in a fall at a business, in a workplace incident, or by a defective product, California law gives you rights and a limited time to use them. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people in Santa Ana with an independent personal injury attorney who understands how Orange County claims and courts work. We are not a law firm; we match you with counsel. There is never a fee unless your case recovers compensation.

whyChoose.title: What Santa Ana injury victims should know

items.title: Usually a 2-year deadline
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file. On a busy corridor like the I-5, camera and vehicle-data evidence can vanish within days.

items.title: Partial fault won't bar recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so pedestrians and drivers alike can recover even when partly at fault; compensation is reduced by your share.

items.title: Claims against the city are different
items.desc: If a public vehicle or hazardous public street is involved, a much shorter deadline — sometimes six months — can apply. Act quickly.

items.title: Orange County experience
items.desc: Your claim runs through the Orange County court system and the insurers active here. We connect you with an attorney who handles these cases locally.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Santa Ana?
items.answer: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years. If a public entity is involved, the deadline can be as short as six months, so speak with an attorney promptly.

items.question: I was a pedestrian and may have been partly at fault. Can I recover?
items.answer: Yes. California's pure comparative fault rule lets you recover even if you shared blame; your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: The case review is free, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — no fee unless they recover compensation for you.

items.question: Where do injury crashes cluster in Santa Ana?
items.answer: Reported-collision records for recent years point to the I-5 (Santa Ana Freeway) and surface routes like First Street and Bristol Street, with crashes peaking on Friday evenings. These are public-record counts, not a verdict about any street.

items.question: Will my case go to trial?
items.answer: Usually not. Most injury claims settle. Your attorney negotiates with the insurer and only litigates if a fair resolution can't be reached.
